members.label: Model D
members.differences: Behringer's copy of the Minimoog Model D, modelled on Moog's 2016 reissue rather than the 1970s original, in a keyboardless case that fits Eurorack. It keeps the three oscillators, oscillator 3 as a modulation source and the two contours, and adds a square and triangle LFO, a switch that turns the 24 dB filter from low-pass to high-pass, patch points, a separate gate input for each contour, decay switches for each, and a chain of up to 16 units for polyphony. A Mod Depth knob stands in for the modulation wheel. One reviewer measured its filter self-oscillating down to about 64 Hz, against about 150 Hz on his vintage Minimoog.

members.label: Minimoog
members.differences: The original, Moog's 1970 portable monosynth: three oscillators, the ladder filter and two contour generators wired together behind the panel, played from its own keyboard with pitch and modulation wheels. Oscillator 3 can be turned into a modulation source.

members.label: Model D (2016)
members.differences: Moog's 2016 rebuild of the Model D on its original sound engine, the version the Behringer copies. It adds a velocity-sensitive keyboard, MIDI, CV outputs, an analogue LFO and the mixer overload modification.
